headline: Median sale prices are up 2.5% YoY nationally; 40 of 50 metros have more price cuts than a year ago.

metric_registry.label: Median sale price
metric_registry.note: Not seasonally adjusted, so compare YoY

metric_registry.label: Sold above list
metric_registry.note: Share of sales above the original list price

metric_registry.label: Listings with price drops
metric_registry.note: Share of active listings with a price drop

brief.text: As of August 2026, the national median sale price rose 2.5% year over year to $399,900, while inventory slipped 0.5% to 1,112,673 listings. The most widespread alert is monthly payments up at least 10% year over year, affecting 39 metros, including Chicago (+15%), Phoenix (+11%), and Dallas (+11%). A second alert shows median prices down at least 3% year over year in 3 metros, led by Austin (-6.6%), Seattle (-4.9%), and Raleigh (-4.4%). Price cuts are more common than a year ago in 40 of the 50 tracked metros, with the national price-drops share at 19.8%, up 0.5pp. The 30-year mortgage rate stands at 7.28%, up 0.25pp over the past week and above last year's 6.34%. Overall, the market temperature reads "Cold" with a score of 19 relative to its own 3-year history.
key_points: Monthly payments up ≥10% YoY in 39 metros, led by Chicago.
Median prices down ≥3% YoY in 3 metros, Austin steepest.
Mortgage rate at 7.28%, up 0.25pp in a week.
